title: Multinomial bound for multicolour Ramsey numbers
statement:
For any natural numbers $k_1, \ldots, k_m$, the multicolour Ramsey number satisfies
\[
r(k_1 + 1, \ldots, k_m + 1) \;\le\; \frac{(k_1 + k_2 + \cdots + k_m)!}{k_1!\, k_2! \cdots k_m!},
\]
the right-hand side being the multinomial coefficient $\binom{k_1 + \cdots + k_m}{k_1, \ldots, k_m}$.
hypotheses_covered: a family of m natural numbers k_1, ..., k_m (indexed by the m colours)
replaced:
\emph{\texttt{r(k$_{1}$+1, \dots{}, k\_m+1) $\le$ (k$_{1}$ + k$_{2}$ + \dots{} + k\_m)!
/ (k$_{1}$! k$_{2}$! $\cdots$
k\_m!)}.}

$r(k_1 + 1, k_2 + 1, \ldots, k_m + 1) \leq \dfrac{(k_1 + k_2 + \ldots + k_m)!}{k_1! \,
k_2! \ldots k_m!}$

Left as exercise 7.2.2 alongside Theorem 7.7, so no book proof.
